agents.expected: the check's operands and a named Java site, so a fix could be attempted
agents.finding: the check stopped at the FIRST fill under a run's corner. A Google export opens with a page-sized white rect and rasterises our bands into images, so white type on an orange band matched the sheet. This run's fix; 5 documents went 42/42.

agents.question: what law does Google use to lay a table row's height, and what LO-invariant change removes the +0.75 pt/row ramp
agents.expected: a law fitted to the committed Google numbers, and one falsifiable change
agents.finding: row = 0.75*round((max(trHeight,content)+rule)/0.75): trHeight is a quantised floor, not a length. 362 is unruled, so it does not ramp +0.75/row - the carry-over's 21.75 pt is ruled-table arithmetic. The LO-invariant change is DocxWriter:6468 declaring the row one rule short; it must be tested on a ruled document, not 362.

context: 18_displacement: the residual on the 13 sole-failure documents is TWO constructs whose errors cancel, and that is why 20 attempts moved 4. Four live Google round trips this slot: med_dy -2.8 (362_price_list_dense), -3.0 (bus-timetable), -6.7 (mobile-bill), -13.0 (72_bank_statement); worst_dy 5.4/4.9/10.0/28.2; med_dx -0.2..+0.2 on all four; bad_pages [0] on all four. Run-by-run profiles: at every table's block top the gap is lost (-8.76, -4.19, -4.08 pt on mobile-bill) and inside every table each row is laid 0.75 pt too tall, so dy climbs back to 0 at the footer. 24 rows x 0.75 = 18 pt of ramp against 17.0 pt of step. Each half refuted alone because spending the spacer overflows (the DocxWriter guard at :6074 names mobile-bill and insurance-policy-schedule) and the row declaration change alone leaves the step uncompensated. The untried pair: deliver the gap through the first-row cell w:before (measured 1:1 by Google, 66 probes, error 0.000000) AND reduce w:trHeight by the same per-row amount, so the table total is unchanged. 362_price_list_dense has no step, only a monotone ramp, so it is the document that proves or refutes the pair. All 13 are converted in /scratch/work/p2w/out.
